title: Novo Nordisk Stock After the Crash: Time to Buy?
creator: The German Value Investor
summary: The German Value Investor critically re-evaluates his Novo Nordisk holding after a ~75% fall from the 2024 all-time high. His community portfolio holds it at an 8.7% weight with an average purchase price of ~EUR44, now trading just under EUR34 (-23%, about -20% with dividends). The setup looks like a bargain at first glance: PE around 10 versus a historical 14-38 range, 4.6% dividend yield, 1.1 trillion DKK market cap, net margins consistently 30-35%, high ROE, foundation ownership and a strong brand — scoring 2.79 in his own stock tool. But the moat is at risk: Wegovy prescription revenue fell ~22% in Q2 2026 after self-pay price cuts ($499 to $349), a US government price agreement, and market-share losses to Eli Lilly (just over 51% to just under 45%); 74% of revenue depends on semaglutide, patents already expired in India, Brazil, Canada and China (generics up to 85% cheaper) with US expiry in 2032; and net cash is negative. His scenarios: bear case fair price 132 DKK (further -50%), base case roughly fair value today, bull case +60% on mid-single-digit growth. After tightening his valuation method, his buying threshold dropped to ~180 DKK — currently 'right at the hold threshold', just below the sell check, with a definite sell zone from 400 DKK. Call: NVO HOLD (first call on record). He closes by plugging his Lululemon crash video (LULU HOLD was Sep 30; no new call here).
